source.title: Probabilistic End-To-End Noise Correction for Learning With Noisy Labels

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates standard cross-entropy baselines under synthetic label noise, reporting test accuracy as the corruption rate varies. It does not report whether those baselines fit the training labels perfectly.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2017) for memorization of random labels, but that cited result is not this study's own result. Its label-estimation figures do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The authors' own cross-entropy baseline experiments test V4's test-error trend across increasing symmetric label noise. They do not establish perfect fitting of the corrupted training labels. Best-versus-last test accuracy alone does not establish V6's ordering of clean-label and noisy-label learning.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that PENCIL corrects noisy labels and improves accuracy and robustness across synthetic and real-world datasets, including clean-data robustness. Qualify this with their reported failure at 80% symmetric noise on CIFAR-100. They do not establish random-label training fit.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates PENCIL, which updates label distributions and uses a staged training procedure; the standard cross-entropy results are baselines. It does not reproduce the random-label experiments in the cited sources.
record.method_sensitivity: For PENCIL, the authors vary noise rate and noise type and report different hyperparameters for CIFAR-10 conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: PENCIL corrects estimated labels and improves noisy-label test accuracy; Figures 2–3 track estimated-label correctness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jointly updating network parameters and label distributions can correct synthetic label noise and improve generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-entropy test accuracy deteriorates between the validation-selected epoch and the final epoch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continued conventional training on noisy labels can worsen clean-test generalization; this does not identify when individual clean and noisy labels are learned.

record.problems: The study reports test accuracy but not training error for its synthetic-noise experiments, so it cannot establish whether the networks fit the corrupted training labels. Some comparison results in Tables 2–4 are quoted from prior work.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: the reported synthetic-noise test accuracies do not establish training-set fitting, required by V4. Label-correction counts in Figures 2 and 3 measure estimated-label correctness, not the claim's training error or generalization behavior. Results in Tables 2–6 compare noisy-label methods and do not test the specified claim versions.

untested.parts: No completely random-label condition or measured training error; unchanged training hyperparameters and chance-level testing after complete randomization are not established.
No comparison of time to fit true versus random labels or convergence speed across corruption rates.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training-set fitting, the fully randomized endpoint, and simultaneous signal learning and noise memorization are not measured.
No relevant removal or comparison of weight decay, dropout, or augmentation.
No separate learning trajectories for clean and corrupted training labels. Declining test accuracy is insufficient to establish their learning order.

missing.what: Extract the authors' own symmetric-noise cross-entropy test accuracies from Table 3. Although explicitly excluded in rows_left_out, these measure V4's test-error component. Keep training fit unmeasured and distinguish validation-selected from final-epoch results.
missing.locator: Section 4.4, Table 3, Cross Entropy Loss; Section 4.4 reports 94.05% accuracy on noise-free CIFAR-10.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 cross-entropy results are quoted from prior work and cannot serve as this study's own evidence. Table 3 results are explicitly from the authors' implementations. Missing training measurements are untested components, not evidence against the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label training, training error, chance-level test error, and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters are not measured.
Training time and convergence speed under random labels or varying corruption are not reported.
No unstructured input conditions are tested.
Test accuracy is reported across synthetic noise rates, but training error is not reported; the claim's perfect training fit and joint train/test pattern therefore cannot be assessed.
The study does not test whether regularization or augmentation prevents random-label fitting or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
The study does not compare the training order or dynamics for real, noisy, and random labels.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, standard cross-entropy baseline, symmetric label noise from 10% to 90%; test-error component only.
relationships.reason: Based on Table 3 text rather than extracted rows: last-epoch test accuracy decreases monotonically from 88.43% through 72.78%, 53.11%, and 33.32% to 16.30%, approaching 10% chance accuracy. Training fit remains untested.
relationships.display_finding: Last-epoch test accuracy declined successively from 88.43% to 72.78%, 53.11%, 33.32%, and 16.30%, approaching 10% chance accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
